2: This Ordinance shall be known as and may be cited as the “Treutlen County Timber Harvesting Ordinance.”
5: All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Treutlen County for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, post or wood chips to any wood yard or processing plant located either in Treutlen County, or anywhere in or outside the State of Georgia must provide notice of such harvesting to the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, or a designated agent, prior to cutting any such timber. Prior written notice is required of any person or firm for each separate tract harvested. Any tract or parcel of timber of sufficient size to require a separate pair of ingress and egress points over a county owned right-of-way shall require a separate notice.
6:
A written notice shall be made upon a form designed and provided by the governing authority of Treutlen County and shall consist of:

- a. A map of the area that identifies the location of the tract to be harvested and the main point of ingress from a public road and the main point of egress to a public road, if different. All points of ingress and egress are subject to the approval of the Treutlen County road department. The Treutlen County Road Superintendent shall make note of any pre-existing problems in these areas.

- b. A statement as to whether the timber will be removed pursuant to a lump sum sale, per unit sale, or owner harvest for the purpose of ad valorem taxation, pursuant to O.C.G.A. §48-5-7.5.

- c. The name, address, and telephone number of the owner of the land and/or timber and the business name, business address, and business telephone number, as well as the cellular and emergency telephone number of the person and/or business harvesting the timber.

2.3 SURETY REQUIREMENT PRIOR TO TIMBER HARVEST. 2.3.1 Amount and Form of Surety.

Each notice of intent to harvest shall not be, or remain, in effect for such harvesting operations unless and until the person or firm providing such notice have delivered to the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, or another designated office, a surety bond in the amount of Five thousand ($5,000.00) dollars, executed by a surety company licensed to do business within the State of Georgia, or at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber, a valid and irrevocable letter of credit, issued by a bank or savings and loan association, in favor of the Treutlen County Board of Commissioners, in the amount of $5,000.00.

2.3.2 Purpose of Surety.

Such bond shall protect Treutlen County against any damage caused by such person or firm, tendering the surety bond or letter of credit, or any agent, employee or contractor of said person or firm and will be used to reimburse Treutlen County for any cost incurred to repair the county maintained right-of-

way, to re-ditch or repair existing ditch structures or for the removal of any harvesting residue, including, but not limited to tree-tops, debris, logs, pulpwood, and other materials placed in or around said right-of-ways. Said bond shall cover all harvesting operations in Treutlen County for that operator unless the bond is forfeited or claimed against the issuer. Said bond shall also be used to offset any cost to maintain or repair any county roads damaged by ingress or egress of trucks engaged in said harvesting operation.

2.3.3 Treutlen County Designee authorized to declare damage and repairs.

The Treutlen County Road Superintendent shall be responsible for the determination of said damages or loss and shall be responsible for determining what repairs or removal may be necessary, in order to comply with the requirements of this Ordinance.

2.34 Opportunity for Timber Harvester to repair damages or loss prior to claim on Surety.

The company responsible for operations under the timber notification will be provided notice of the damage and allowed three (3) business days (being Monday through Friday) to restore the road, and/or ditch, or removal of debris, to a safe and operable condition, as determined by the Treutlen County Road Supervisor, prior to any claim on the surety bond or letter or credit. All repairs, materials used and schedules undertaken to make any necessary repairs shall be conducted under the sole discretion and supervision of the Treutlen County Road Superintendent. The timber operator shall be solely responsible for any cost associated with signing, closing, or using the equipment made necessary for the repair of the road and/or ditch.

2.3.5 Requirement of additional Surety upon the claim of existing Surety.

If any surety bond or letter of credit is held, claimed against, or forfeited for any amount to reimburse Treutlen County for such damages, then any notice that is dependent on said bond shall not be, or remain, in effect for such harvesting operations, unless and until the person or firm shall cause to be delivered to Treutlen County a separate surety bond or letter of credit in the amount of $5,000.00.

For purposes of this section any such surety bond or letter of credit may be valid and applicable to subsequent timber harvests in Treutlen County, provided that such surety bond or letter of credit has not expired. Additionally, any such surety bond or letter of credit that has been properly delivered to

t

Treutlen County may be applied to and shall satisfy multiple timber harvest that a timber harvester may have ongoing at any particular time in Treutlen County.

2.3.6 Effective term of notice.

Any notice of harvest provided to Treutlen County shall be effective for such timber harvesting operation on said tract upon the receipt of the same by the governing authority of Treutlen County or its designated agent and upon compliance with the requirements set forth in this Ordinance and at a time when said notice is posted at the harvesting site and until said time that the harvester gives notice as to the completion of said harvest to the governing authority of Treutlen County. Any material change in information provided on said notice must be submitted to the governing authority within three (3) business days.

2.3.7 Release of Surety.
7: The surety bond or letter of credit may be released by the governing authority of Treutlen County upon notification of completion of harvesting activities by the person or firm harvesting said tract and only upon final inspection of the harvesting site, points of ingress and egress, and all affected rights-of-ways and ditches leading to and from the harvesting site by the designee of the governing authority of Treutlen County and/or the Treutlen County Road Superintendent. The timber harvester, at its option, may choose to allow the surety bond or letter of credit to be retained by Treutlen County, for application against future timber harvesting operations.
8:
3.1 Jurisdiction and Venue of Violations.

Violation of the notice requirements shall be prosecuted in the State Court of Treutlen County, Georgia.

3.2. Amount of Fine upon Conviction.

Upon conviction, a violator shall be subject to a fine, not to exceed Five hundred ($500.00) dollars per violation.

3.3. Separate offense for each day of harvest in violation.

Each day of operation of a timber harvest, without the required notice and posting of a surety bond and/or letter of credit shall constitute a new and separate offense of this ordinance.
10: The regulations expressed in this document shall be considered as the minimum provisions for the protection of the health, safety, economy, good order, appearance, convenience, and welfare of the general public of Treutlen County, Georgia. The governing authority of Treutlen County may subsequently amend this Ordinance.
11: Whenever the requirements made under authority of this Ordinance impose higher standards than are required in any other statute of local ordinance or regulation, provisions of this Ordinance shall govern.
12: Should any section or provision of this Ordinance be declared by the courts to be unconstitutional or invalid, such a declaration shall not affect the Ordinance as a whole, or any other part thereof other than the part as declared to be unconstitutional or invalid.
13: All Ordinances, or parts of ordinances in conflict with any of the provisions of this Ordinance are hereby repealed.
14:
This Ordinance shall take effect and be in full force on and after the date that it is enacted by the governing authority and published in the legal organ of said county for four weeks.

Adopted, approved, and enacted this 1st day of November, 2011, at the Regular Meeting of the Board of Commissioners of Treutlen County, Georgia.
